newsitem.title: GREECE: GREECE'S MINOAN LINES LAUNCHES $110 MLN FERRY.
newsitem.headline: GREECE'S MINOAN LINES LAUNCHES $110 MLN FERRY.

text.p: Passenger shipper Minoan Lines launched on Monday the high-speed ferry (HSF) Ikarus which is expected to enter service on Greece-Italy sea routes in January 1998.
Minoan Lines in a statement the vessel was launched in Brucess Shipyards in Landskrona, Sweden in a ceremony attended by Greek government and shipping officials.
It will be transported to Fosen Shipyards in Trodenheim, Norway for completion.
Technical characteristics of HSFs include a gross registered tonnage of 31,000 tonnes and a speed of 27 knots.
Their passenger capacity stands at 1,500, plus 700 beds and aircraft-type seats.
The Patras-Ancona service which takes 19 hours competes with services run by Attica Enterprises, Strintzis Lines and unlisted ANEK Lines.
The ship will also be servicing the Patras-Venice and Patras-Brindisi routes at projected journey times of 23 and 9 hours, respectively, Minoan Lines said.
In the coming two weeks, construction of HSF Pasiphae, the sister ship of HSF Ikarus, will commence at the Brucess Shipyards.
HSF Pasiphae will be delivered in April 1998.
The total cost of Ikarus and Pasiphae reached $220 million, financed at 70 percent by a pool loan syndicated by Citibank's shipping division. The remainder has been met by equity.
In September 1996, Minoan Lines successfully completed a 19.5 million dollar share capital increase.
Minoan Lines announced a 59.5 percent increase in net profit to $18 million in 1996.
Gross operating income rose 16 percent to $121 million, while net profits before depreciation were up 40 percent to $26 million, it said.
Minoan Lines said booking figures in 1997 exhibited growth.
Over the first four months of 1997, bookings for the Greece-Italy route were up 30 percent while operating income was 31.5 percent higher at $14.1 million.
Over the same period, operating income from domestic services grew 16.4 percent to $5.7 million dollars. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
